profile.summary: RoseTTAFold All-Atom predicts the structure of a biomolecular assembly from its parts. Inputs are given per chain: protein sequences as FASTA, nucleic acid strands as DNA or RNA FASTA, small molecules as SDF files, plus covalent bonds between a protein chain and a small molecule. The output is a PDB file with predicted lDDT in the B-factor column and a separate PyTorch file of confidence metrics, of which the developers' main one is pae_inter, the mean error of protein residues with respect to atom frames together with atom coordinates with respect to protein frames. They warn that the model is not accurate for all cases and say the error estimates are there to let users tell the good predictions from the bad, with pae_inter below 10 expected to mean a high quality dock.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: header, Inference Configs Using Hydra and Understanding model outputs

summary_quotes.text: RoseTTAFold All-Atom is a biomolecular structure prediction neural network that can predict a broad range of biomolecular assemblies including proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, covalent modifications and metals
RFAA is not accurate for all cases, but produces useful error estimates to allow users to identify accurate predictions.

- PDB file with predicted structure (bfactors represent predicted lddt at each position)
- pytorch file with confidence metrics stored
This was the primary confidence metric we used in the paper and expect cases with pae_inter <10 to have high quality docks.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Inference is driven by Hydra configuration files: a job inherits the base configuration and adds one entry per chain under protein_inputs, na_inputs, sm_inputs and covale_inputs. Alignments and templates are built by a script against UniRef30, BFD and a 2021 March snapshot of PDB100. The network settings in rf2aa/config/inference/base.yaml, the only model configuration in the sources read, sit under the key legacy_model_param and describe a RoseTTAFold style stack: 4 extra blocks, 32 main blocks and 4 refinement blocks, with MSA channels 256, full MSA channels 64, pair channels 192 and template channels 64, and SE(3) transformer layers of 32 channels and 2 degrees for structure refinement. It uses atom frames, chirality and Lennard-Jones terms. At inference the loader keeps up to 128 latent and 1,024 total alignment sequences and 4 templates, and recycles 4 times by default. The developers recommend keeping the defaults because they match the training task, but say raising MAXCYCLE to 10 gives better results on hard cases.
sections.source_locator: base.yaml: loader_params and legacy_model_param; README: Inference Configs Using Hydra and Setup

quotes.text: We highly suggest using the default parameters since those are closest to the training task for RFAA but we have found that increasing loader_params.MAXCYCLE=10 (default set to 4) gives better results for hard cases (as noted in the paper).

The main inputs into the model are split into:
- protein inputs (protein_inputs)
- nucleic acid inputs (na_inputs)
- small molecule inputs (sm_inputs)

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One released checkpoint, RFAA_paper_weights.pt, downloaded from files.ipd.uw.edu and named as checkpoint_path in the default configuration. The sources read list no other weights, and the developers say they will share new models as they create them. Reproducibility also depends on the databases, which are pinned by name: UniRef30_2020_06, BFD, and PDB100 at 2021 March 03, plus legacy BLAST 2.2.26. A result should name the checkpoint, the repository commit, the MAXCYCLE setting and the database versions, and should state whether signalp6 was installed, since the Docker route leaves it out for licensing reasons and the predictions then do not use it.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: All-atom biomolecular structure prediction network for assemblies of proteins, nucleic acids, small molecules, covalent modifications and metals.

quotes.text: a biomolecular structure prediction neural network that can predict a broad range of biomolecular assemblies

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: RoseTTAFold style three-track network with SE(3) transformer refinement. The only model configuration in the sources read, the legacy_model_param block of base.yaml, gives 4 extra blocks, 32 main blocks and 4 refinement blocks, MSA dimension 256, pair dimension 192 and template dimension 64, with atom frames so that ligand atoms are treated as nodes.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A Hydra configuration naming, per chain: protein FASTA files, nucleic acid FASTA files with input type dna or rna, small molecule SDF files, and covalent bonds between protein and small molecule chains. A chain letter for each entry is required.
facts.source_locator: README: Inference Configs Using Hydra, Predicting Protein Monomers and Predicting Protein Nucleic Acid Complexes; base.yaml: input keys

quotes.text: This represents a chain letter and is absolutely **required**, this is important when users are specifying multiple chains.
In this case, the allowed input types are dna and rna.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Two files: a PDB file whose B-factors hold the predicted lDDT per position, and a PyTorch file of confidence metrics, which include per-node plddts, an L by L pae matrix, an L by L pde matrix, and the means mean_plddt, mean_pae, pae_prot and pae_inter.

quotes.text: 2. pae, a LxL tensor where the model predicts the error of every j position if the ith position's frame is aligned (or atom frame for atom nodes)
7. pae_inter, the mean over all the errors of protein residues with respect to atom frames and atom coordinates with respect to protein frames.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not stated. The sources read give the block counts and channel widths in the configuration but no parameter count for the checkpoint.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Not stated in the sources read. The repository describes the databases used at inference, UniRef30 2020_06, BFD and PDB100 from 2021 March 03, but says nothing about what the released weights were trained on; the paper was not fetched.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: One released checkpoint, RFAA_paper_weights.pt, the weights used in the paper. The developers say new models will be shared as they are made, and point to RF-NA for paired protein-RNA alignments and to RFdiffusionAA as the related design model.

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not stated by the developers in the sources read. The repository pins database snapshots for inference, UniRef30 2020_06 and PDB100 at 2021 March 03, which are not training cutoffs.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: No stated maximum assembly size. The limits in the configuration are on the alignment and templates: 1,024 alignment sequences, 128 latent sequences and 4 templates, with 4 recycles by default and 10 suggested for hard cases.

run_guide.summary: Build the environment, download the weights and databases, and predict the bundled protein monomer example.
prerequisites: A Linux machine with an NVIDIA GPU and drivers, as the Docker instructions require.
Mamba or Miniforge, and Python 3.10 as pinned in environment.yaml.
About 400 GB of disk for UniRef30 (46 GB), BFD (272 GB) and the PDB100 templates (81 GB), plus the legacy BLAST binary.
A separately licensed copy of signalp6 from https://services.healthtech.dtu.dk/services/SignalP-6.0/, for the full input pipeline.
BSD 3-Clause terms, which the licence states cover the weights as well as the code.

notes: The record came from the LiPP lipid-protein benchmark (existing source evidence-expansion-p2-lipp-2026-6ff34f2f709a), which reports a 2020-04-30 training cutoff for RoseTTAFold All-Atom in its Table 1. The developers' own files read here do not state a training cutoff or a training set, so this page records those as not extracted rather than repeating the benchmark's figure; the Science paper would settle it but is not openly fetchable and has no PMC copy. The repository is rf2aa in its module names and RoseTTAFold-All-Atom in its address. GitHub reports the licence as NOASSERTION, but the LICENSE file is a BSD 3-Clause text that says in terms that it covers the weights as well as the code. The block counts and channel widths come from the legacy_model_param key of rf2aa/config/inference/base.yaml, the only model configuration in the sources read; no saved file states that the released checkpoint uses that parameter set.
